Little Jimmy Johnson, entitled and spoiled as he is, finally drove his mother crazy - to the point of threatening him with a summer with Uncle Bob, in Uncle Bob's forest cabin. Unphased, Little Jimmy Johnson continued to whine and cry and act out, until Mommy Johnson just couldn't take it anymore. "Off with you!" she cried, pushing his pleading, crying sixteen year old self onto a boarding plane, "One summer living without your toys, if that doesn't teach you a lesson, I don't know what will!"

Skip ahead a day or two, and we see Little Jimmy Johnson sitting on the porch of Uncle Bob's cabin, power-cycling his iPhone repeatedly. Over and over and over, the same message appears: No Service Available. His cries and murmurs of "not fair" have been grating on Uncle Bob's nerves now, and despite every offer of activity, Little Jimmy Johnson seems content to be discontent. Not fishing, not hiking, not mending the fences, nothing would stir Little Jimmy Johnson from his brooding emo fit.

"How 'bout huntin'? You wanna go huntin'?" Uncle Bob is at the end of his rope already, mere days into this ordeal. Little Jimmy Johnson looked up, mascara running down his acme-riddled cheeks.

"Hunting? You mean... like with a gun?"

Uncle Bob lit up, he'd found his 'eureka' activity! "Of course, 'with a gun.' Tell you what, my Pappy used to send me out by myself with a pocket-full of .22 rounds, I'd spend all day out there in these woods and I have to say - it's some of the better memories I ever did have out there. Finding myself, y'know?" Little Jimmy Johnson warmed to the idea, and for the first time this trip, put his iPhone away. Uncle Bob dug out his old .22 rifle and a box of rounds - shoved the rifle in his face, gave him a quick run-down of operations (each step cut off and interrupted by "yeah, yeah, I know Uncle Bob" and maybe even an eye-roll or two.)

Off to the woods, Uncle Bob offered his last piece of advice to the young, wayward teen - "Stick to the path, and watch out for the black bear!" Little Jimmy Johnson didn't need advice.

About an hour or so after starting his walk, and a few popped - errant shots at some startled squirrels, the appeal of "hunting" and being out in the woods started to wane. He turned, griping about how 'stupid' and 'lame' this was, when movement in the brush ahead of him caught his eye. He raised the rifle quickly, and popped off a few rounds, one of them hitting an old, abandoned beehive and sending dust and mud particles thickly into the air. He waved it away to find his prize - whatever it was that he shot. Nothing.

Suddenly - he felt a strong tapping on his shoulder. Tap tap tap. He turned, and there before him stood a massive black bear, towering above him. This wasn't just an ordinary, run of the mill black bear - this black bear talked. He spoke to the frozen-in-fear emo kid, "You took a shot at me. Now I get to take a shot at you."

The bear pounced down on him, flipped him onto his belly, and rutted him good.

In shock and absolute disbelief, shame and anger, Little Jimmy Johnson hobbled home back to Uncle Bob's cabin, and prepared to face the music. In the confusion, he'd left the .22 rifle in the woods - he was injured in more ways than he could have ever imagined before coming to these infernal woods. When he got to the cabin, he was surprised to find a note pinned on the door.

'Jimmy, out fishing, be back later tonight. - Uncle Bob.'

After sulking and trying to mend the superficial wounds the bear's claws made, the feeling of anger and shame grew and intensified. 'How dare that bear do that to me?! I should kill that bear. I should kill the shit out of that bear!' he thought, checking his service status on his iPhone again (there was still none.) Finally, the plan hatched itself in his head - he'd get revenge over this bear's... actions. He was going to actually man up and hunt this predator down.

Digging around in Uncle Bob's attic revealed a big old double barrelled shotgun and a handful of shells. He loaded it up and put on an old Hunter's Jacket, and charged out the front door with a mission at the forefront of his mind. He was going to kill that bear.

An hour or so after walking, and finding the .22, he was coming up short. Nothing. When a little flicker of movement in his peripheral vision tweaked his attention, Little Jimmy Johnson spun quickly - raised the shotgun, screamed "Fuck you, Bear! Die!!" and let loose with both barrels. BOOM, BOOM! The dust was thick and blinding, and a small sapling of a tree fell to the ground in splinters. Little Jimmy Johnson beamed with pride - surely, this killed that bear!

Tap, tap, tap.

Screaming and fighting did nothing, he was simply no match for the bear - as once again it pinned him down, clawed at his back, and this time Little Jimmy Johnson swore he heard the bear actually laugh as he rutted away, taking his "shot" in return. A playful paw to the back of the head and with a crunch-snap-crash - the bear was gone. Little Jimmy Johnson sobbed silently in the middle of the woods - never before feeling so ashamed, so beaten and defeated.

A single spark of ultimate rage filled his chest. He was determined now, more than ever, to end this bear. The little pea-shooter didn't do anything, and this shitty old shotgun was obviously defective - he was going to have to find Uncle Bob's big guns.

Arriving at the still-empty cabin, Little Jimmy Johnson flung the door open, nearly breaking it off the hinges. Through tears in his eyes, he dug around under Uncle Bob's bed - coming up with a large, highly-sophisticated and modern looking rifle with a magazine of rounds that looked bigger than chicken tenders. "Aha!" he screamed with pride, anger and frustration in a delightful mix, "Fuck you, bear, you're going DOWN!" He picked his pace up to nearly a full-on run as he tore out of the cabin and back into the woods.

Step by step, his eyes and ears worked in a sync that he never would have guessed - he wasn't just out for fun, to pop off at squirrels, or to knock over tin cans - he was hunting. Every snap and break of a twig was aimed at, every nuance and ever-so-slight movement drew immediate, trained attention towards it.

Finally, after a good, long while, he spied his nemesis - the black bear - scratching it's back on an old standing-dead Oak tree. It grinded up against it roughly, wood splinters and broken twigs falling in an orchestra of noise.

Little Jimmy Johnson took aim with the massively heavy firearm, using the advanced zoom scope to bead the crosshairs directly on the bear's chest. 'There's no way I'm missing this time,' he thought to himself, watching the bear in his sights, and waiting for the right moment, 'This bear is as good... as... dead.'

KABOOM! The rifle let off a report that was so loud and powerful that it knocked Little Jimmy Johnson over himself, dropping the rifle and sending a flock of nearby birds into an absolute panic. He collected himself and waved the dust away as quickly as he could, coughing all the while. The dead-standing tree was obliterated, nothing left except toothpick-sized scraps littering the entire forest around it.

But no bear.

Tap. Tap. Tap.

Utterly crushed, Little Jimmy Johnson just gave up and exploded into tears. His shoulders slumped and big, fat tears fell to the ground. He sobbed and looked up at the bear now standing fully upright on it's hind legs, but mere feet away from him.

"You know," the bear began, "I have a feeling you're not out here for the sport of it."

Fast forward to today. The only games I really play are Hearthstone (Magic the Gathering is too expensive and the online client sucks), Diablo 3 and Fallout 4. Previous to these I liked Skyrim, Mass Effect 1 2 and 3, GTA 4, and Battlefield 3.

I have come to enjoy Diablo and Fallout less and less each time I play them. I find I don't have enough time to grind Diablo to push the high grifts my friends are doing. I like Fallout 4 still, but I can't get into it in the short hour I can find to play when the kids are in bed and my wife is doing her facebook stuff. It just isn't enough time to immerse in the world and truly appreciate everything. I haven't even installed a mod yet!

Now to the realization, aside from Hearthstone, which I can hop in and out of quickly, play a few fun games or whatever whenever I can find time, I think I am playing the wrong type of games.

Something that I can play in 20-30 minutes and have a good time. My phone: I hate free to play/freemium/microtransactions. This is funny because I llike Hearthstone. My laptop: Old Dell XPS 15 with an Nvidia GT420M. It now runs Linux Mint. It can play Hearthstone and Diablo 3 in wine. I also like it for Civ 5, but time constraints make that a difficult game to play.

My Desktop: Dual boot, runs Linux Mint 95% of the time. Only boots into Windows 7 with zero updates and all Windows 10 features blocked for Fallout 4.

It's not that I don't have time; I put in hard work through the day and into the evenings, and I sacrifice a lot of sleep - but that's another can of worms. I think it's because of all the anxiety that gets heaped on you as a parent, provider and so on.

That probably doesn't make sense, so here's an example situation. It's 10pm. My son is finally asleep, my wife is spending time with her mother downstairs in the in-law suite, watching something on Netflix. I'm in my office, loading up Pillars of Eternity, Party Hard, Banished or something else that's got my interest lately. I notice that my cup is almost out of drinking water, so I get up and go to the kitchen. I notice dog toys out on the way, so I pick them up. Then I see cat toys out of place, so I pick them up and put them away. The rug is all janked up from one beast or another tearing around the house, so I straighten that out. While I've taken a knee doing that, I notice clothes that need sorting balled up in a corner. The laundry isn't being done, so I start doing that. The dryer's lint trap is full; so is the trash can in the office, and kitchen. Fourty-five minutes later, I'm standing - in my slippers, house-shorts and a slightly dirtier t-shirt - outside. I'm holding a bag of trash in the bitter cold and I'm looking back at my house and thinking about shoveling some snow when it occurs to me "hey, weren't you supposed to be relaxing?" followed by "at least that hunted, anxious feeling has been somewhat satisfied with all your chore busywork."

We're not 17 and sinking that 400th hour into The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, or playing another late night round of slappers only in the library anymore, OP. It's bittersweet, but I suppose that gamers are not immune to the nebulous notion of growing up. My one glimmer of hope has been setting content aside for my son when, if he chooses to take up the hobby when he's old enough. YMMV, and I wish these subjective experiences of mine didn't speak to me of personal truths that I'd rather not acknowledge; and yet, here I am, oversharing.

Oddjob is still god damned bullshit, though.

I tend to avoid single player games and ones where you don't do much other than just sit there with you and yourself at the keyboard controls. I'm the kind of person who thinks "what am I getting out of this, other than enjoyment?" Also, much of the time, little enjoyment is had if the game is centered around "leveling up". Many people will probably disagree with that, but I'm not saying to avoid those games.

But I think at least one of your primary games should involve talking to people.

That may sound like something that would make you uncomfortable, but the rewards are something that most games fail to give.

If you're curious, I play games like Grand Theft Auto, but almost exclusively online. There's so much fun you can have by talking. And, like most people, I use my voice a lot in the real world, and these games have helped me develop speaking skills which are applicable in the real world. I can make friends in the real world easily just by using the right voice. And it doesn't require lying. It's mostly the tone and pace that people pick up on, and less of what is actually said. Practicing your voice is something I wish more people would do because it makes this idea make more sense. I think with any games you play, speaking to other players should be a part of at least one. Even if you're insecure about your voice, I think you would be surprised by how you can improve it, simply by making an effort to use it. Do you have an insufferable vocal fry? Work on it by talking online. When I was younger (around 12) I'd play GTA 4 and very often people would be annoyed by my voice, but the worst thing I could have done is give up, and unplug the mic like many people do. I worked on not sounding like such a 12 year old, and through that I experience I gained useful skills.

Probably 90% of my gaming experience has been in either GTA 4, RDR, or GTA 5- all in their online modes. I think what I'm doing may sound a bit crazy to people, but it has really benefited me and in ways you may not believe. I think I'm playing the right games.
